newsitem.title: USA: Lott assumes US cap gains tax cut to about 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Lott assumes US cap gains tax cut to about 20 pct.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Tuesday he assumed that a capital gains tax cut to about 20 percent for the maximum rate would be included in tax legislation being crafted.
The Mississippi Republican said he spoke with House Speaker Newt Gingrich, a Georgia Republican, "in general terms" Monday about the tax bill being drafted in the House.

"I'd like to see it down around the 20 percent," Lott said, for the capital gains tax rate cut from the current maximum of 28 percent. Asked if he believed that was what would be in the tax bill, Lott replied: "I would assume so."
Lott told reporters he had spoken with Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth, a Delaware Republican, Monday about a possible schedule for the tax legislation.

Roth was hopeful the Finance Committee would complete consideration of the spending bill around June 17 or 18 and the tax bill around June 20 and then the legislation could be considered in the Senate the week of June 23, Lott said.
"We would like, if at all possible, to get both reconciliation bills through the House and the Senate before the Fourth of July," Lott said.
